title: Phenotypic persistence versus resistance versus latency
dek: Persisters are genetically drug-susceptible cells that survive a pulse of antibiotic by being temporarily non-growing or tolerant. Resistance is a heritable MIC shift. LTBI is a clinical label. Do not fuse the three.
story: A biphasic kill curve is the laboratory handle on phenotypic persistence: a fast death of the replicating bulk, then a shallow tail of survivors that, once drug is removed and growth resumes, yield colonies that are still drug-susceptible on a MIC plate. Those survivors are persisters. Their children are not a resistant clone. The genotype did not buy the tail; a physiologic state did (slow or no replication, a stressed envelope, a DosR-high programme — the latency-and-DosR plate is that physiology).

Genetic resistance is a different object: a heritable change (rpoB S450L, katG S315T, pncA LOF) that shifts the MIC of the lineage, not of one stressed cell for one afternoon. You can select resistant mutants from a large replicating population while a persister subpopulation is sitting through the same drug pulse without a new SNP. Relapse after apparently adequate therapy can be reconstitution from persisters, a missed resistant subclone, or reinfection — those are three hypotheses, not one word.

Latent TB infection (LTBI) is an immune-operational category: a positive IGRA or TST after active disease has been excluded. It does not prove a named caseum full of Wayne-model persisters, and a negative IGRA does not prove sterility. TPT is a low-burden bet. Treating a cavity as if it were a persister tail with two weekly drugs is the category error the LTBI plate already forbids.
deepTitle: Kill curves, mutation supply, and the words people smash
deep: Tolerance versus resistance: tolerance is slower kill at a concentration that still exceeds the MIC; resistance is a higher MIC. Persistence is a subpopulation phenomenon (heterogeneous survival) rather than a uniform shift of the whole culture’s MIC. A “tolerant strain” with a longer minimum duration of killing is related but not identical to a stochastic persister fraction.

Mutation supply scales with N × μ among cells that replicate. A tiny non-replicating tail contributes little new resistance during the pulse; the replicating bulk is where rpoB mutants are born. That is why combination therapy and burden matter even when a persister story is true.

Models: Wayne hypoxic shift-down, nutrient starvation, caseum surrogates, and hollow-fibre hollow the same word “dormant” at different oxygen, lipid, and pH settings. PZA’s special reputation is partly “activity on non-replicators in acid.” None of those models is a DST catalogue.

Do not write “MDR persister” unless you measured a resistant genotype and a phenotypic tail. MDR is a DST/genome claim. Persister is a kill-curve claim. LTBI is a clinic claim. The DosR regulon is a transcription claim. Four vocabularies, four assays.

Serial isolates that stay genotypically susceptible after failure push you toward persistence, inadequate drug exposure, or a sampling miss — not toward inventing a new rpoB codon in the methods sentence.

visual.caption: Four layers people collapse into one adjective. Top: a clinical LTBI label. Next: physiologic non-replication (hypoxia, caseum, DosR). Next: a phenotypic persister tail on a kill curve, still genetically susceptible. Bottom: heritable resistance that moves the MIC. Relatedness is conceptual, not a developmental pathway you can assume in one patient.

example.title: A surviving tail that still looks wild-type on DST
example.setup: Hollow-fibre or flask: 10⁸ CFU, rifampin well above the WT MIC. After a steep 2-log drop, a tail of ~10⁴ CFU holds. Colonies from the tail have a wild-type rpoB and a WT MIC. A colleague files them as “rifampin resistant persisters.”

steps.title: Name the tail
steps.body: 10⁴ / 10⁸ = 10⁻⁴ of the inoculum survived the pulse and grew out susceptible. That is a persister fraction, not a resistance frequency. Call it phenotypic persistence.

steps.title: Where resistance would have lived
steps.body: Pre-existing rpoB mutants, if present at ~10⁻⁸, would be ~10 cells in 10⁸ — a different pile, and their progeny would fail a MIC test. Mixing the piles is how “the tail proves MDR” gets written.

steps.title: What you still do not know
steps.body: Whether those persisters were DosR-high, lipid-loaded, or simply non-growing is a physiology experiment (latency-DosR plate), not a consequence of the kill curve alone. Whether the patient has LTBI is a clinic experiment, not this flask.

example.takeaway: A drug-S tail is persistence. A heritable MIC shift is resistance. IGRA+ is LTBI. Assay each.

check.prompt: Phenotypic persisters, in the sense of this plate, are best described as:
choices: Cells whose progeny show a stably elevated MIC because of a resistance mutation
A subpopulation that survives a lethal antibiotic pulse without a heritable MIC shift — genetically susceptible on regrowth
Any isolate with a DosR gene present (it is core)
check.answer: A subpopulation that survives a lethal antibiotic pulse without a heritable MIC shift — genetically susceptible on regrowth
check.why: The defining lab picture is a kill-curve tail whose colonies remain drug-S. Resistance and LTBI are other layers.

whyWrong.Anyone with a positive IGRA: That is the LTBI operational label, not a flask persister assay.
whyWrong.Any isolate with a DosR gene present (it: DosR is nearly universal in MTBC; presence of the gene is not a persister phenotype.

check.prompt: Inoculum 10⁸ CFU, persister fraction 10⁻⁴, resistance mutation rate ~10⁻⁸ per replication to a named rpoB codon. Order-of-magnitude counts in the starting flask:
choices: ~10⁴ persisters and ~10 pre-existing resistant mutants — different piles
The two counts must be equal by definition
check.answer: ~10⁴ persisters and ~10 pre-existing resistant mutants — different piles
check.why: 10⁸ × 10⁻⁴ = 10⁴ phenotypic survivors if that fraction is persisters. 10⁸ × 10⁻⁸ = 10 expected resistant mutants if that μ applies to the replicating pool. They are not interchangeable.

whyWrong.~10⁸ persisters and ~10⁸ resistant mutan: That would be the whole culture twice.
whyWrong.The two counts must be equal by definiti: The whole point of the plate is that they are not the same definition.

check.prompt: On the hierarchy plate, a wild-type MIC after a kill-curve tail belongs in which layer?
check.figureHint: Four stacked layers from LTBI down to genetic resistance.
choices: They are all the same layer
check.why: Drug-S progeny after a tail is the persister layer. A heritable MIC shift would sit one layer down; IGRA+ sits at the top.

whyWrong.They are all the same layer: The plate exists because they are not.
